claim: The case involved animal rights protester Elliot Katz, who filed a Bivens action against military police officer Donald Saucier.
evidence: Katz brought an action in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California against Saucier and other officials pursuant to Bivens v. Six Unknown Named Agents, alleging that the defendants had violated his Fourth Amendment rights by using excessive force to arrest him.
excerpt: While Vice President Al Gore began giving a speech, Katz removed the banner from his jacket, started to unfold it, and walked toward the fence and speakers' platform. Petitioner Donald Saucier, a military police officer on duty that day, had been warned by his superiors of the possibility of demonstrations with Katz being previously identified as a potential protester. Saucier and Sergeant Steven Parker, another military police officer, moved to intercept Katz as he walked toward the fence.
